questions.q: Write the number of donor atoms present in EDTA during the formation of the complex.
questions.solution:
Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) is a hexadentate ligand, meaning it has six donor atoms that participate in the formation of a complex.

Complex Formation:

  • EDTA can chelate metal ions by donating electron pairs from these six donor atoms, forming a stable octahedral complex.
  • It is widely used in analytical chemistry, medicine, and industrial applications for metal ion sequestration.

questions.q:
Write the formula to calculate EAN.



Explain the formation of [CO(NH3)6]3+ complex ions with respect to the type of hybridisation.



Explain the formation of [CO(NH3)6]3+ complex ions with respect to magnetic property.
questions.solution:
EAN = Number of electrons of metal ion + total number of electrons donated by ligands

= Atomic number of metal (Z) – Number of electrons lost by metal to form the ion (X) + Number of electrons donated by ligands (Y)

= Z – X + Y



The complex ion [CO(NH3)6]3+ is an example of a coordination complex where cobalt (CO3+) is the central metal ion and six NH3 ligands surround it.

  • The oxidation state of CO in [CO(NH3)6]3+ is +3.
  • The electronic configuration of CO (Z = 27) is [Ar] 3d7 4s2.
  • CO3+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d6.
  • Since NH3 is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of electrons in the 3d orbitals.
  • This leads to d2sp3 hybridization, forming an octahedral geometry.


The complex ion [CO(NH3)6]3+ is an example of a coordination complex where cobalt (CO3+) is the central metal ion, and six NH3 ligands surround it.

  • After pairing, all six electrons occupy the lower energy t2g orbitals (low-spin complex).
  • Since there are no unpaired electrons, the complex is diamagnetic in nature.

Thus, [CO(NH3)6]3+ has d2sp3 hybridization and is diamagnetic.

questions.q: Calculate effective atomic number of \[\ce{[Co(NH3)6]^3+}\] ion.
questions.solution:
The oxidation state of Co is +3, and ligands donate 12 electrons.

Z = 27, X = 3, Y = 12

EAN of \[\ce{Co^3+}\] = Z –  X + Y

= 27 – 3 + (2 × 6)

= 27 – 3 + (12)

= 36

EAN of \[\ce{[Co(NH3)6]^3+}\] in is 36.

questions.q: What is Nessler’s reagent?
questions.solution:
• Nessler's reagent is a solution of mercury(II) iodide (HgI2) in potassium iodide (KI) and potassium hydroxide (KOH) named after the German chemist Julius Nessler.
  • Nessler’s reagent is an alkaline solution of K2 HgI4.
  • It is used in testing for ammonia, with which it forms a brown colouration or precipitate.

\[\ce{NH3 + 2[HgI4]^2- + 4OH^- → HgO.Hg(NH2) + 7I^- + 3H2O}\]

  • Low ammonia: Yellow coloration

  • High ammonia: Reddish-brown precipitate

This color change confirms the presence of ammonia.

questions.q: Fe2+ ions react with nitric oxide formed from reduction of nitrate and yields a brown  coloured complex _____________.
questions.solution:
[ Fe(H2O)5NO ]2+
 An aqueous salt solution containing nitrate ion is mixed with ferrous sulphate and sulphuric acid solution. First nitric oxide  is formed.
NaNO3 + H2SO4 → NaHSO4 + HNO3

6FeSO4 + 3H2SO4 + 2HNO3 → 3Fe2(SO4)3 + 4H2O + 2NO

 Fe2+ ions react with nitric oxide formed from reduction of nitrate and yields a brown coloured complex [Fe(H2O)5NO]2+

Thus, one mole of ferrous sulphate reacts with one mole of nitric oxide and five moles of water to form the complex [Fe(H2O)5NO]2+
The balanced chemical reaction is shown below.
FeSO4 + NO + 5H2O → [ Fe(H2O)5NO]SO4
This reaction is used for the detection of nitrate ion in the ring test.

questions.q: Explain cationic, anionic and neutral sphere complexes w ith example.
questions.solution:
1. Cationic Complexes: A cationic sphere complex is a coordination compound with a positively charged coordination sphere.

For example: \[\ce{[Co (NH3)5Cl] SO4 ⇌ (Co (NH3)5Cl)^{2+} + SO^{2-}_{4}}\]

2. Anionic Sphere Complexes: An anionic complex is a coordination compound with a negatively charged coordination sphere.

For example: \[\ce{[Ni(CN)4]^{2-} K3[Fe(CN)6] ⇌  3K^{+} + [Fe(CN)6]^{3-}}\]

3. Neutral Sphere Complexes: A neutral coordination complex lacks cationic or anionic spheres.

For example: \[\ce{[Pt (NH3)2 Cl2] , [Ni (Co)4]}\]

questions.q: What is effective atomic number? Calculate effective atomic number of copper  ( Z = 29 ) in (Cu ( NH3)4)2+
questions.solution:
Effective atomic number (EAN) in a complex is defined as the total number of electrons present around the central metal ion.

EAN = Atomic number (Z) – Oxidation number + 2 × Coardination number

Let us consider a chemical complex [Cu(NH3)4]2+

The atomic number of the central metal atom (Cu) Z = 29

Oxidation number = +2

Coordination number = 4

EAN = 29 – 2 + (2 × 4)

EAN = 29 – 2 + 8

EAN = 35

questions.q:
What is ‘effective atomic number’ (EAN)?



Calculate the effective atomic number of the central metal atom in the following  compounds:

K4Fe(CN)6  Fe(Z=26)



Calculate the effective atomic number of the central metal atom in the following  compounds:

Cr(CO)6 Cr(Z=24)
questions.solution:
It is total number of electrons around the central metal ion present in a complex and calculated as the sum of electrons on the metal ion and the number of electrons donated by ligands. It can be calculated using formula,
EAN =Z-X+Y
where Z = Atomic number of metal.
X = Number of electrons lost during the formation of metal ion from its atom.
Y = Number of electrons donated by the ligands. 



K4Fe(CN)6

Z=26, X=2,Y=12

EAN=Z-X+Y=26-2+12=36



Cr(CO)6

Z=24, X=0,Y=12

EAN=Z-X+Y=24-0+12=36
